assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned a superconducting circuit into a controllable artificial atom strongly coupled to a single microwave photon, giving dispersive qubit readout, quantum buses and the architecture of present superconducting processors. It is original, clearly defined and demonstrably foundational for a whole technology, and it is distinct from the 2025 prize, which honoured macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in circuits rather than light-matter coupling and control.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the Wallraff et al. strong-coupling experiment in Schoelkopf's group are the decisive pair. Blais as lead theorist, Schoelkopf as group leader and Wallraff as first experimentalist form a coherent three-person configuration. Girvin's theoretical role is substantial and omitting him is a real allocation problem; the choice between Girvin and Blais is not settled by the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly mature: reproduced in many laboratories, two decades of widespread use, commercial and academic processors built on it. Timing is natural, though a prize this soon after the 2025 superconducting-circuit award could be judged as too close to the same field.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants another superconducting-circuit prize immediately after 2025.
Fair split of credit among Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff, plus earlier cavity-QED precursors.
I work in this area, so my own judgement of its importance should be read with that in mind; I have not independently verified dates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance showed that quantum information can be protected in principle, which is what makes large-scale quantum computing a coherent goal. Shor's nine-qubit code and Steane's CSS-type codes opened the field, and Kitaev's toric code and anyon-based fault tolerance connect it to topological order. The conceptual impact on both information science and condensed matter is very large.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently found the first codes in 1995-96 and Kitaev introduced topological codes. Others who made decisive contributions, for example the threshold theorem authors and Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill and Laflamme, are not in the supplied credit, so the three-name configuration is incomplete as a history. Shor's factoring algorithm is not part of this candidate and should be kept separate.
assessment.maturity: The theory is mature and experimental demonstrations of logical qubits, including recent below-threshold surface-code results, are encouraging but still early. Recognising the concept now seems defensible; an experimental-validation emphasis would be premature.
uncertainties: Credit among the many contributors to codes and the threshold theorem is contested.
Practical scalability of fault-tolerant machines is not yet established, to my knowledge.
Possible overlap with a separate quantum-algorithm or computing candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a new and tunable platform for correlated and topological phases. The idea is simple, original and has generated a large field with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the 2011 continuum theory of the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. Cao and co-authors, and the group of Dean and others on related moire systems, are not all in the credit, so the experimental side may need a broader or different allocation. The three supplied names support a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups, but the field is still evolving rapidly and the understanding of the superconductivity is not settled. Recognition would be timely but somewhat early with respect to the interpretation.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene remains debated.
Credit for the experimental discovery beyond the supplied names, and the earlier theory by others on twisted layers.
Whether the field's maturity is sufficient.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new classification of band structures by topology, with protected edge and surface states. The theory, followed by the HgTe quantum well observation, changed the way matter is understood and is a worthy continuation of the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz line.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the key Z2 theory and Molenkamp's group the first experimental realisation in HgTe, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. The supplied credit omits Mele, Hasan and the BHZ theorists, and one of the BHZ authors is deceased. The Kane plus Molenkamp pair is the most defensible two-person option from the given names, but it leaves Mele out and this is a genuine allocation problem. Xue's quantum anomalous Hall work belongs to a separate candidate.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well confirmed, with many materials and a mature theory. Timing is more than adequate; the difficulty is attribution rather than maturity.
uncertainties: Allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and BHZ-related names.
Overlap with the separate time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum anomalous Hall candidates.
Technological impact is limited so far, to my knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-type models with controllable parameters, including the superfluid-Mott insulator transition, fermionic Mott states and single-site resolved quantum gas microscopes. This created quantum simulation as a laboratory discipline and has addressed strongly correlated many-body problems.
assessment.attribution: Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger carried out the decisive lattice experiments with fermions and bosons and with microscopy. Cirac and Zoller are credited for the theoretical proposals, and Jaksch et al. is the Bose-Hubbard proposal; the theory-experiment balance is a real question and the three-name experimental set leaves out foundational theory. The Nobel committee has already honoured Bose-Einstein condensation and optical trapping.
assessment.maturity: Experiments are widely reproduced and the field is mature, though demonstrated simulation beyond classical reach is still a goal. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation between theorists (Zoller, Cirac) and experimentalists.
Overlap with Rydberg-array and trapped-ion candidates.
Degree to which simulation has yielded new physical insight rather than demonstration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for ion-trap quantum gates and its experimental realisation produced the first mature platform for quantum computation, with the highest-fidelity gates and algorithms demonstrated on small processors. Original and conceptually important; it complements QEC and circuits.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the 1995 scheme and Blatt's group realised gates and entanglement with many ions. Wineland and Monroe also contributed greatly to ion-trap experiments and gate development; Wineland's 2012 prize already honoured ion manipulation, so the credit may be split and Monroe is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is strong and independent across several groups. The concept is mature, but the practical computing outcome is not yet decided.
uncertainties: Role of Wineland's and Monroe's work relative to the credited names.
Overlap with the optical-lattice candidate where Cirac and Zoller also appear.
Uncertainty about the outcome of scalable ion-trap computing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and associations with a blazar flare and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy as a new window. The experimental conception of a cubic-kilometre ice detector was bold and the results have lasting astrophysical impact.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the credited originator and leader of the IceCube concept. Because the discovery is the product of a large collaboration, and because other pioneers of large-volume neutrino detection (for example the DUMAND and AMANDA predecessors) are not in the supplied credit, a one-person prize is difficult to justify. I note I cannot propose other names.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established and independent follow-up is limited to date, and source identification beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 is still developing. Recognition would be early to fairly timely.
uncertainties: Prize-configuration problem with a single credited name and a large collaboration.
Independent confirmation by KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD is limited so far, to my knowledge.
Source associations are still few.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model's particle content and required technical achievements in detectors and data analysis of the highest order. Importance and clarity are beyond doubt, and the 2013 prize recognised the theory but not the experiments.
assessment.attribution: The supplied names are the founding and leadership figures of ATLAS and CMS. Whether leadership of collaborations of thousands is the proper basis for an award is a statutes and allocation problem, as many individuals made decisive contributions; this makes a fair three-person configuration hard to defend.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed with precision coupling measurements by two independent experiments. Timing is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Attribution to collaboration leaders instead of the many contributors is contested.
Whether the committee views the 2013 prize as having already settled the Higgs recognition.
The supplied credit may not reflect who made the decisive analysis contributions.
